exact_rationales./research_rationale: EO 13792 (signed 2017-04-26, 82 FR 20429-20431), read in full from the held FR text, orders the Secretary of the Interior to review Antiquities Act monument designations made since 1996 (sec. 2(a)-(c)) and report to the President, an interim report within 45 days and a final report within 120 days (sec. 2(d)-(e)). The machine own-term kinds are report_deadline (sec. 2(d), 2(e)) and condition (sec. 3(b)). A report deadline is never an end; the order has no sunset or termination wording, so every clause remains part of the order until revoked. No clause's first end needs a report date, so the order is not blocked on the report-deadline question; the producer does not claim when either report was delivered. EO 13990 (86 FR 7037-7043, read in full; reading record scale/readings/LSP-EO_13990.json) sec. 7(a) revokes it, effective on signing, 2021-01-20. The dossier lists no missing provision and no other actor provision; a by-number scan of all 6,652 held FR-original texts finds EO 13792 named only in EO 13990. The monument-boundary proclamations of 2017 were separate Presidential acts, not part of this order. EO 14148 and EO 14154 (2025) revoke EO 13990 but name none of the six orders and reinstate nothing. Inventory: the dossier's 18 clauses cover the operative text from sec. 1 through sec. 3(c); its scope labels for sec. 2(a)(v)-(vii) ('sec2-v', 'sec2-v-vi', 'sec2-v-vii') are irregular but each span is correct and no text is missing or duplicated.

final_report_identity.quote:
I. Introduction and Purpose 
As described more fully below, Executive Order 13792, "Presidential Executive Order on the 
Review of Designations Under the Antiquities Act," dated April 26, 2017, (Order or EO 13792) 
directed me to conduct a review of certain Presidential designations made under the Act, to 
determine if the designations conform to the policies set forth in the Order. The Order further 
instructed me to provide two reports summarizing this review: 
a. an Interim Report under section 2(d), due within 45 days, addressing the Bears Ears 
National Monument established by Proclamation No . 9558, dated December 28, 2016, 
and "other such designations as the Secretary determines to be appropriate for inclusion"; 
and 
b. a Final Report under section 2(e), due within 120 days, summarizing the findings of the 
review for all other monument designations covered by the Order. 
The Order also requested that I include in both reports recommendations for "Presidential 
actions, legislative proposals, or other actions consistent with law" to conform designations to 
the policy set forth in the Order. 
This Memorandum constitutes the Final Report under section 2( e) of the Order and addresses the 
findings of the review of certain Presidential designations made under the Act.

final_report_goal.quote:
The final step was to 
review policies on public access, hunting and fishing rights, traditional use such as timber 
production and grazing, economic and environmental impacts, and potential legal conflicts, and 
to provide a report to you no later than August 24, 2017.

final_report_further_measures.quote:
Specific monument modification measures will be submitted separately should you concur with

final_report_ongoing.quote:
I therefore recommend ongoing review of monuments to ensure that while continuing to protect 
objects, the proclamations prioritize public access; infrastructure upgrades, repair, and 
maintenance; traditional use; tribal cultural use; and hunting and fishing rights. 
D. Management Plans 
The DOI heard from many stakeholders that its management plans associated with monuments 
are restrictive and difficult to navigate . When monuments are designated, the underlying land 
ownership remains, typically including the applicable management authorities associated with 
the land-managing agency. The overriding management framework then becomes the protection 
of the objects of historic or scientific interest. However, there is discretion in this management 
"overlay," and the DOI review reveals that this requirement has at times been too strictly 
interpreted to impede allowable uses under management plans. The DOI plans to undertake a 
review of existing monument management plans and update them with those considerations in 
mind. The DOI believes this can be done in a manner that is consistent with public access, 
infrastructure, traditional use, tribal cultural use, and hunting and fishing rights.

testimony_submission.quote: In response to strong local concerns about egregious past abuses of the Act, President Trump signed Executive Order 13792 on April 26, 2017, which tasked the Secretary to conduct a review of all Presidential designations or expansions of designations under the Antiquities Act since January 1, 1996, that exceeded 100,000 acres, or any others that were made without coordination and outreach to the public. The Secretary, in accordance with the Executive Order, submitted two reports for consideration to the President. The first was an Interim Report specifically addressing the Bears Ears National Monument. The Final Report features an assessment of 27 monuments, which was informed by travel to eight monument sites; dozens of meetings with stakeholders, ranging from tribal, local, and state officials to conservation organizations; and the first ever formal comment period tied to the Antiquities Act.

source_findings.conclusion: Original sec2(d) requires an interim report on Bears Ears and other designations chosen by the Secretary; sec2(e) independently requires a final report summarizing the review. Both require recommendations and provision to the President through the OMB Director, Assistants for Economic and Domestic Policy, and CEQ Chairman. Neither is a recurring reporting schedule.

DOI testimony affirmatively reports an Interim Report specifically on Bears Ears was submitted to the President. This supports actual occurrence by 2018-01-30 independently of the Final Report. The interim document is not among these inputs; contents, date and required routing cannot be fully verified here. Final-report identity alone would not prove the interim duty was performed.

Rendered final-report page 3 confirms this memorandum expressly constitutes the sec2(e) Final Report. Rendered page 1 confirms memorandum for the President from Ryan K. Zinke, signature image, and final-report subject, with no visible date. Testimony attests a Final Report assessing 27 monuments was actually submitted to the President by 2018-01-30. The testimony does not fingerprint the exact revised PDF transmitted, specify transmission/receipt date, or prove passage through every required official; final page cc lists those officials but is not a receipt record.

45-day and 120-day terms fix duties/deadlines and do not prove performance or cessation. The report mentions a goal of providing a report no later than 2017-08-24; it does not say in that passage that delivery occurred that day. The dated 2018 testimony supplies affirmative retrospective occurrence evidence, not an exact delivery date or a timeliness finding.

EO13792 is dated/signed April 26 2017; filing April 28 and FR publication May 1 are separate later documentary events. It contains no separate delayed effective date; its reporting periods run from the date of the order. These dates cannot be substituted for actual report performance. EO13990 revocation signing/effective timing is asserted by the claim; this bounded review neither replaces nor independently reauthenticates that later-actor conclusion.

Original sec2(a) review and sec2(b)-(c) consultation, policy and sec3 qualifications must be considered apart from one-time report provision. The final report contemplates separate monument modification measures, recommends ongoing monument review, and states plans for management-plan review/updates and congressional action. Recommendations or agency plans do not by themselves extend EO13792 or create new EO commands. The original preserves statutory agency authority and OMB functions, requires lawful appropriated implementation, and disclaims enforceable rights. A reporting event proves neither whole-order cessation nor the extinction of independently authorized later acts.
